title: Capability-bound host parity
summary: Add one trusted HostCapabilitySnapshot and one canonical output/receipt pipeline so native hooks, repository fallback, Claude workflows, Claude Tasks, Codex tasks, evaluator output, lifecycle stops, routing, and token telemetry vary only by transport while retaining the existing ReviewKernel and orchestrator/human authorities.

current_state.summary: The accepted ReviewKernel already supplies immutable envelopes, scoped views, leases, producer/write observations, taskplane.lens-slot-output/v2 collection, and canonical revisions. Host-dependent seams remain inconsistent: Codex packages native hooks and also installs a repository bridge; onboarding equates matching files with readiness; Claude review/evaluate workflows validate a legacy findings shape; bounded eval adapters do not declare native output schemas or a governed-file fallback; Stop/SubagentStop do not validate exact worker submissions; tier routing can emit unverified host values; and cached-token parsing is not provider-semantic. The external current-state inventory is empty, so these premises are grounded directly in the cited repository and accepted decisions 0005/0006.

alternatives.name: One capability snapshot and canonical contracts
alternatives.description: Derive one versioned, source-attributed HostCapabilitySnapshot and use it to select hook, schema, and routing transports; require every transport to converge on canonical output validation, ReviewKernel collection, submission validation, host receipts, and provider-normalized telemetry.

gains: One host-neutral authority with deterministic fallbacks and shared negative fixtures
Preserves accepted ReviewKernel leases, result schema, collector, and revision identity
Makes unsupported, unknown, contradictory, inherit, and unavailable states explicit
costs: Adds two focused cross-cutting modules and versioned migration records
Requires coordinated adoption across hooks, workflows, adapters, lifecycle, routing, recorder, tests, and docs
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Revisit the module split if capability and output contracts stabilize with fewer than two consumers each, or if a supported host exposes a single authoritative cross-product capability and receipt API.

alternatives.name: Patch each host path independently
alternatives.description: Keep native Codex hooks, the repository bridge, Claude workflows, Task dispatch, eval adapters, and token readers as separate authorities and add local guards to each.

gains: Smaller initial diffs in each subsystem
costs: Preserves duplicated schemas, capability guesses, retry rules, and evidence authorities
Cannot mechanically prove semantic parity or prevent future transport drift
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Revisit only if cross-host equivalence is explicitly removed from product scope and each host is allowed a different governance meaning.

alternatives.name: Require native capabilities and remove fallbacks
alternatives.description: Accept only native plugin hooks, native structured output, and exact native model/effort controls; reject all repository, file-validation, inherit, and unsupported host paths.

costs: Excludes older, unknown, managed, read-only, or policy-restricted supported hosts
Contradicts the explicit fallback and portability acceptance criteria
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Revisit after every supported Claude and Codex version plus managed deployment guarantees native hooks, structured output, model control, effort control, and effective receipts.

decision: Select capability-contract because R-0006 changes five cross-host contracts and requires equivalent evidence under unsupported and unknown capabilities. It is the only option that extends accepted decision 0005's host-neutral ReviewKernel instead of creating parallel hook, findings, submission, dispatch, or telemetry authorities. Two focused modules keep capability detection and output validation out of the already-large CLI, kernel, and transport adapters; every new module traces to multiple acceptance criteria and has a named owner and rollback boundary.

contracts.description: Versioned capability state, native-preferred/bridge-fallback selection, stable event identity, exactly-once claim/replay, truthful onboarding, and read-only submission-aware Stop/SubagentStop decisions.

Claude workflow and Task/Codex transports consume the existing immutable envelope, view, routing, lease, producer, exact result path, taskplane.lens-slot-output/v2 schema, host write receipt, collector, and canonical revision without a parallel findings convention.

Each evaluator dispatch declares one strict versioned schema, exact output path and attempt bound; native structured output and host-observed governed-file fallback converge on the same validator before record, collection, submission, or gate.

Abstract tiers resolve only through host capabilities to exact, inherit, unsupported_fallback, or pre-dispatch block; planned and host-observed model/effort remain separate and provider ids never cross hosts.

Versioned bounded lifecycle events and provider-normalized token usage report attempts, transports, validation, receipts, availability and cache categories without prompts, full transcripts, command arguments, secrets, credentials, or double counting.

risks.risk: A host capability probe can become a new false authority if it trusts model prose, file presence, or stale configuration.
risks.mitigation: Accept only bounded host/version probes, policy/trust facts and host-observed load/child/write receipts; carry source/confidence and treat unknown/contradictory as fallback or block.

risks.risk: Both loaded hook paths can race and produce inconsistent allow/deny results.
risks.mitigation: Use one exclusive stable-event claim and response replay; require a fresh session when no stable event identity exists; test concurrent duplicates under the host timeout.

risks.risk: Workflow resume can reuse semantically stale evidence despite a valid cached return value.
risks.mitigation: Bind cache identity to target/context/view/lease/schema/slot/producer/revision and revalidate canonical file plus host write receipt before reuse; allow one retry only.

risks.risk: A generic configured model name can accidentally match a foreign provider or unsupported old-host option.
risks.mitigation: Resolve through host-scoped alias/effort capability rows; pass only supported non-null values; strict blocks and non-strict records inherit/unsupported_fallback.

risks.risk: Lifecycle leak recovery can destroy a valid or missing governed submission before validation.
risks.mitigation: Submission-required slots are never PID/TTL auto-released and Stop/SubagentStop are read-only; only orchestrator/human release after the gate.

risks.risk: Provider usage semantics or duplicate rows can fabricate low cost or double count cache input.
risks.mitigation: Use provider-specific normalizers, single-sourced weights, stable event ids, reconciliation equations and unavailable status for ambiguous/corrupt data.

risks.risk: Cross-cutting work can weaken currently green CI while fixing the three named failures.
risks.mitigation: Keep existing jobs and assertions as floors, add focused negative/mutation tests first, compare test manifests, then require the complete unchanged matrix.

risks.risk: The compatibility bridge becomes permanent duplicated surface.
risks.mitigation: Track explicit debt and remove only after two supported releases show universal native hook load receipts across managed deployments.

failure_modes.mode: Native and bridge hook paths are both loaded for one event.
failure_modes.detection: hook_event signal reports duplicate claim for the same stable digest.
failure_modes.recovery: The kernel owner replays the first completed safe response within 2 seconds, records one effective execution, and onboarding migrates only taskPlane-owned bridge rows for the next session.

failure_modes.mode: Trust, managed policy, load state, or stable event identity is unknown or contradictory.
failure_modes.detection: host_capability signal reports unknown or contradictory status with source and confidence.
failure_modes.recovery: Onboarding selects no unproved path, preserves settings, and tells the user whether a fresh session or administrator action is required; it never suggests bypass.

failure_modes.mode: Native or file-fallback evaluator output is malformed, wrong-version, oversized, extra-field, or unobserved.
failure_modes.detection: evaluation_attempt signal reports validation failure code and bounded diagnostic.
failure_modes.recovery: The evaluation driver retries once with the same schema and write scope, then terminates failed and admits no evidence to record, collection, submission, or gate.

failure_modes.mode: A workflow cache identity or leased slot producer/write receipt is stale or mismatched.
failure_modes.detection: review_slot_validation signal reports the mismatched target/context/view/lease/schema/slot/producer/revision field.
failure_modes.recovery: The workflow owner invalidates that cache entry, performs at most one fresh child attempt, and leaves canonical collection incomplete on repeated failure.

failure_modes.mode: Stop or SubagentStop sees no valid submission for its exact governed slot.
failure_modes.detection: submission_stop_check signal reports contract, workspace, task, stage, slot and missing artifact/status.
failure_modes.recovery: The lifecycle hook blocks and tells the worker to retry the exact submission or return to the orchestrator/human; it leaves contract, loop state, results, siblings and submission bytes unchanged.

failure_modes.mode: An explicit model or effort route cannot be honored by the current host.
failure_modes.detection: dispatch_route signal reports unsupported_fallback or mismatch between planned and host-observed receipt.
failure_modes.recovery: Strict mode blocks before child start; warn/default mode inherits with an explicit reason and exact_route_verified=false, then the dispatch owner may correct host-scoped configuration.

failure_modes.mode: Token usage is absent, negative, corrupt, duplicated without identity, or irreconcilable with provider totals.
failure_modes.detection: token_usage signal reports unavailable and a provider-specific reconciliation reason.
failure_modes.recovery: The recorder keeps workflow and structural gates active, marks token comparison unavailable/not_comparable, and asks the evaluation owner to repair telemetry; it records no fabricated zero.

failure_modes.mode: Runtime guidance fires before an engine-authored evidence bundle has proved acceptance.
failure_modes.detection: evaluation_attempt signal contains both runtime-guidance and unproven-criterion diagnostic codes.
failure_modes.recovery: The evaluator applies the bounded correction, but the loop still refuses pass until each criterion is proved; the orchestrator sees both diagnostics and state does not advance.

failure_modes.mode: A rollout phase breaks a previously green host, package, docs, release, or dispatch job.
failure_modes.detection: ci_regression signal names the failed existing job and test-floor diff.
failure_modes.recovery: The release owner stops the phase and rolls back only its transport selection while retaining exactly-once, schema validation, submission preservation and fail-closed rules; in-flight identities finish or cancel without translation.

signals: host_capability signal: versioned status, source, confidence, fingerprint and bounded reason per capability
hook_event signal: effective path, stable digest, first-or-duplicate claim, response class and exactly-one side-effect count
evaluation_attempt signal: stable run/attempt id, transport, schema path, timing, terminal status, validation and bounded diagnostic codes
review_slot_validation signal: target/context/view/lease/schema/slot/producer/revision match and host-observed write result
submission_stop_check signal: exact workspace/task/stage/slot, submission status, missing artifact and read-only block/allow decision
dispatch_route signal: tier, capability source, planned model/effort, passed arguments, host-observed model/effort, resolution and exact verification
token_usage signal: provider, category totals, raw/effective reconciliation, availability, reason and dedup count
ci_regression signal: pinned failure status, existing job status and test-manifest/floor diff
alerts: Block the affected hook/evaluation/submission/gate and surface one actionable recovery when capability authority, event identity, schema validation, slot provenance, explicit strict route, or governed submission cannot be proved.
Mark token comparison unavailable/not_comparable, without blocking absolute workflow and structural gates, when provider usage cannot be reconciled.
Stop rollout when any existing green CI job or test floor regresses.
observability.privacy: Persist no prompt, full transcript, command argument, secret, credential, or unnecessary absolute user path. Diagnostics are code plus at most 512 redacted bytes; large outputs are represented by repository-relative governed path, digest, and byte count.

rollout.strategy: Four additive gates: (1) ship strict readers/validators and shadow HostCapabilitySnapshot/route/telemetry records; (2) enable exactly-once hook claims and native-preferred truthful onboarding while preserving the observed current-session path; (3) move workflows, evaluator adapters and Stop/SubagentStop to canonical schema/submission validation; (4) enable strict explicit-route enforcement, refresh only the tp-go fingerprint, compose both runtime and DoD diagnostics, then require focused negative/mutation suites and the complete unchanged CI matrix. Legacy ReviewKernel v2 results remain v2 and bridge migration edits only taskPlane-owned rows.
rollout.rollback: Rollback may change only transport selection: native hooks may fall back to a trusted, policy-permitted, loaded bridge with exactly-once claims; model/effort may fall back to explicit inherit only in non-strict mode. It may never accept prose/unvalidated JSON, clear submission-required contracts, translate in-flight leases/revisions/output schemas, or drop host receipts and redaction. If no governed fallback exists, fail closed; preserve append-only lifecycle/usage records and cancel/restart incompatible in-flight runs.

visualization.reason: The data-flow makes the selected authority boundary visible: three capability-dependent transport branches converge on one output/receipt path, while submission-aware Stop blocks without clearing or gating.

lens_evidence.evidence: Checked direct as-built sources because the inventory is empty; preserved accepted ReviewKernel decision 0005; compared canonical, host-local and native-only alternatives; traced all new modules and five changed contracts to the 14 exact acceptance criteria; set numeric hook/output/retry/privacy bounds; bound failure detection to declared signals and bounded owners/recovery; made rollout and rollback schema/submission safe; named owners, sequencing, fixtures, compatibility debt and the exact three CI failures plus green floors. No material Build decision or open product question remains.
